9. PW 1 in his evidence, by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A has deposed that on 07.09.2018, at about 09.30 P.M, he was coming to his house, from Sector14, Dwarka New Delhi.

He has deposed that when he was crossing the road near Kautilya Apartment, Sector14, Dwarka, New Delhi, a car bearing No. DL1RTB7671 being driven by R.1 came from the side of Dwarka More in a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner, on wrong side of the road, hit him.
He has deposed that as a result of which he fell down on road and received fracture and other multiple grievous injuries all over his body.
He was taken to Venkteshwar Hospital Dwarka New Delhi for his treatment where he was operated upon.
He has deposed that he was shifted to Base Hospital N Delhi for his further treatment.
He has suffered 5% Permanent physical disability due to injuries received in this accident.

sentences.text: Being injured, the petitioner was the natural eye witness of the accident.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338/427 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
11.The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by his medical documents.
After investigation, police indicted respondent no. 1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority, against his alleged false implication, if any.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.1 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of car bearing No. DL1RTB7671 by respondent no. 1 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.

When he ( petitioner ) was crossing the road near Kautilya Apartment, Sector14, Dwarka,

As a result of which he fell down on road and received fracture and other Surender Singh Bisht vs Pushp Kumar @ Abhishek on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136036547/
He was taken to Venkteshwar Hospital Dwarka New Delhi for his treatment where he was operated upon.

There was no Zebra crossing or any sign of stopping of vehicles on the road from which petitioner was crossing the road.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338/427 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
After investigation, police indicted respondent no. 1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority, against his alleged false implication, if any.

So this Tribunal while taking the middle path and taken into consideration of Minimum Wages Act at the time of accident, has assessed the income of injured as Rs.15,000/ p.m. So seeing the nature of injuries ( fractured in left leg) on the person of petitioner, which may took considerable time to heal up.
His ability to earn in future has to be kept in mind while awarding compensation to injured.
However he has not filed any documents with regard to his earning.
Counting in this way, his loss to future earnings comes to Rs.

Seeing age and occupation of petitioner, his functional disability is taken as 03% qua the whole body.
This amount of Rs. 37,800/ is allowed to petitioner, as loss of future earnings, due to permanent disability.
